blocks.text: 8. Completely Erasing Good and Evil

inline.s: The Master saw that the followers of the various schools, given to difficult questioning, had all stirred up malicious minds and gathered in great numbers beneath his seat. Moved to compassion, he said to them: “Those who study the Way should altogether wipe out all good thought and evil thought. Being nameless, name it after the self-nature; the non-dual nature is called the true nature. Upon that true nature all the teaching-gates are established, and at the very words you must see it for yourselves.” Hearing this, the assembled people all paid their respects, requesting to serve the Master as their teacher.

blocks.text: Chapter Nine: The Chapter on Protecting the Dharma
1. The Speedy Edict Summoning the Master

inline.s: On the festival of the first full moon of the first year of the Shenlong era, Empress Wu Zetian and Emperor Zhongzong issued an edict saying: “We have invited the two masters An and Xiu to be supported in the palace. In the leisure of the myriad affairs of state, We constantly investigate the One Vehicle. The two masters deferring, said: ‘In the south there is a Chan master Neng, who received in secret the robe and the Dharma of the great master Ren and transmits the Buddha’s mind-seal; he may be invited and questioned.’ Now We send the inner attendant Xue Jian with a speeding edict to invite you. We beg the Master, in his compassion, to come quickly to the capital.” The Master presented a memorial declining on the ground of illness, wishing to end his days amid the forests and hills.

blocks.text: 2. Sitting in Meditation and Entering Concentration

inline.s: Xue Jian said: “The Chan worthies of the capital all say: ‘To attain the Way one must sit in meditation and enter concentration; one who is liberated without relying on meditation and concentration has never existed.’ We have not yet heard what Dharma the Master teaches.” The Master said: “The Way is awakened to by the mind — how could it be in sitting? The Sutra says: If one says the Tathagata sits or lies down, he is practicing an erroneous path. Why? Since he has no coming from anywhere and no going to anywhere. No arising and no ceasing — this is the Tathagata’s pure meditation. All dharmas are empty and still — this is the Tathagata’s pure sitting. In the ultimate there is nothing to realize; how much less so a mere sitting!”

blocks.text: 3. Pointing Out the Essence of the Mind

inline.s: Xue Jian said: “When the disciple returns to the capital, the sovereign will certainly question me. I beg the Master, in his compassion, to point out the essence of the mind, so that I may transmit and report it to the two palaces and to those in the capital who study the Way. It is like one lamp lighting a hundred thousand lamps: the dark ones are all illuminated, and the illumination is endless.” The Master said: “The Way has neither brightness nor darkness; brightness and darkness are the meaning of mutual alternation. That the illumination is endless is also to call it finite, because the name is established in mutual dependence. The Vimalakirti Sutra says: The Dharma has no comparison, because it has nothing to depend upon.”

Xue Jian said: “Brightness is the metaphor for wisdom, and darkness for affliction. If a person who cultivates the Way does not use wisdom to break through affliction, then on what can he rely to escape the beginningless birth and death?” The Master said: “Affliction is itself bodhi; they are not two and not separate. To use wisdom to break affliction — this is the view of the two vehicles, the capacity of the goat and the deer. Superior wisdom and great faculties are altogether not like this.” Xue Jian said: “What is the view of the Mahayana?” The Master said: “Brightness and non-brightness: the ordinary person sees them as two; the wise know thoroughly that their nature is not dual. The non-dual nature is the true nature. The true nature is not diminished amid the common and foolish, not increased in the sage and worthy; abiding amid affliction it is not disturbed, dwelling in concentration it is not stilled. It is neither interrupted nor eternal, neither coming nor going, neither within the middle nor without and within, neither arising nor ceasing. Nature and marks are as such, abiding and unchanging — this is called the Way.”

Xue Jian said: “The Master speaks of no arising and no ceasing — how is this different from the heresy of the externalists?” The Master said: “What the externalists call no arising and no ceasing is to use ceasing to stop arising and to use arising to reveal ceasing: their ceasing is still not ceasing, and their arising they call not arising. What I call no arising and no ceasing is: originally there was no arising, and now there is no ceasing, and therefore it is different from the externalists. If you wish to know the essence of the mind, do but refrain from thinking of any good or evil, and you will naturally enter the pure essence of mind, serene and eternally still, with its wonderful functions as numerous as the sands of the Ganges.” Xue Jian, having received the instruction, was suddenly and completely enlightened; he bowed, took leave, and returned to the palace, presenting the Master’s words in his memorial.

blocks.text: 4. An Edict of Commendation

inline.s: On the third day of the ninth month of that year, an edict commended the Master, saying: “The Master has declined on account of old age and illness, and, cultivating the Way for Us, is a field of blessing for the nation. The Master, like Vimalakirti, feigning illness at Vaishali, has proclaimed the Mahayana, transmitted the mind of all Buddhas, and spoken the Dharma of non-duality. Xue Jian transmitted the Master’s instruction on the Tathagata’s knowledge and vision. We have gathered the surplus blessings of accumulated virtue and planted the roots of goodness in past lives; encountering the Master’s appearance in the world, We suddenly awaken to the Supreme Vehicle. Mindful of the Master’s grace, We bow our heads in endless gratitude! And We offer the woolen kasaya and the crystal bowl, and command the prefect of Shaozhou to restore the monastery buildings and present the Master’s former dwelling as the Guoen (Nation’s Grace) monastery.”

blocks.text: Chapter Ten: The Chapter of Entrustment
1. Teaching You to Speak the Dharma

inline.s: One day the Master called his disciples Fahai, Zhicheng, Fada, Shenhui, Zhichang, Zhitong, Zhizhe, Zhidao, Fazhen, and Faru, and said: “You are not like the rest of people; after my nirvana, each of you will be a master of one direction. I now teach you to speak the Dharma so as not to lose the fundamental school. First you must raise the three categories of dharmas, employ the thirty-six pairs of opposites, and in going out and coming in remain far from the two extremes; in expounding all dharmas do not depart from the self-nature. If someone suddenly asks you about the Dharma, let your words be in pairs, always taking up the dharma of the opposites, with coming and going mutually dependent; in the end the two dharmas are entirely done away with, and there is nowhere further to go.”

blocks.text: 2. The Three Categories of Dharmas

inline.s: The three categories of dharmas are the aggregates, the realms, and the entrances. The aggregates are the five aggregates, namely form, feeling, thought, mental formations, and consciousness. The entrances are the twelve entrances: the six external sense-dusts — form, sound, smell, taste, touch, and dharma; and the six internal gates — eye, ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind. The realms are the eighteen realms: the six sense-dusts, the six gates, and the six consciousnesses.

The self-nature can contain the myriad dharmas; this is called the alaya (store-house) consciousness. If thinking arises, this is the evolving consciousness. From it arise the six consciousnesses, which go out through the six gates and see the six sense-dusts; thus the eighteen realms all function from the self-nature. If the self-nature is evil, there arise eighteen evils; if the self-nature is right, there arise eighteen rightnesses. If one uses it in evil, it is the use of sentient beings; if one uses it in good, it is the use of the Buddha. Of what does the use consist? Of the self-nature itself.

blocks.text: 3. The Thirty-Six Pairs of Opposites

inline.s: The dharma of the opposites. Five pairs of the insentient external realms: with heaven, with earth; with sun, with moon; with brightness, with darkness; with yin, with yang; with water, with fire — these are the five pairs.

Twelve pairs of dharma-marks and language: with words, with dharma; with being, with nonbeing; with possessing form, with formlessness; with possessing marks, with marklessness; with the defiled, with the undefiled; with form, with emptiness; with motion, with stillness; with purity, with turbidity; with the ordinary, with the holy; with monks, with laypeople; with old, with young; with great, with small — these are the twelve pairs.

Nineteen pairs in the functions of the self-nature: with long, with short; with evil, with right; with delusion, with wisdom; with foolish, with wise; with confusion, with concentration; with compassion, with malice; with precepts, with non-precepts; with straight, with crooked; with real, with false; with dangerous, with level; with affliction, with bodhi; with constant, with inconstant; with pity, with harm; with joy, with anger; with renunciation, with stinginess; with advance, with retreat; with arising, with ceasing; with the Dharma-body, with the physical body; with the transformation-body, with the reward-body — these are the nineteen pairs.”

The Master said: “If you understand how to employ these thirty-six pairs of opposites, then the Way will be threaded through all the scriptures and dharmas, and in going out and coming in you will be far from the two extremes. When the self-nature functions and you converse with others, be apart from marks amid outer marks, and be apart from emptiness amid inner emptiness. If you cling entirely to marks, you will grow erroneous views; if you hold entirely to emptiness, you will grow ignorance. A person who holds to emptiness slanders the scriptures, flatly saying there is no need of words. Since he says there is no need of words, then people should not speak at all — for this very speech is the mark of words. Again he says: ‘The direct way establishes no words.’ But these very two characters ‘no words’ are themselves words. When he sees what others say, he immediately slanders them as clinging to words. You should know that to be deluded oneself is one thing, but to slander the Buddha’s scriptures is another. Do not slander the scriptures, for the offense and hindrance are immeasurable!”

If one clings to marks outside and does work to seek the true, or widely builds up teaching grounds and speaks of the faults of being and nonbeing, such a person will not see the nature even over many kalpas. Just listen and practice in accord with the Dharma, and do not cease to think of the hundred things and thereby obstruct the way-nature. If you listen and do not practice, you will cause people to give rise to false thoughts. Just practice in accord with the Dharma and give the Dharma-gift without dwelling on marks. If you awaken, and speak thus, use thus, practice thus, and act thus, you will not lose the fundamental school.

If someone asks you about the meaning: when asked about being, answer with nonbeing; when asked about nonbeing, answer with being; when asked about the ordinary, answer with the holy; when asked about the holy, answer with the ordinary. The two paths are mutually dependent, and the meaning of the Middle Way is produced. As with one question answered with one pair, all remaining questions are handled in this manner, and you will not lose the principle. Suppose someone asks: ‘What is meant by darkness?’ Answer: Brightness is the cause and darkness the condition; when brightness ceases there is darkness. Use brightness to reveal darkness and darkness to reveal brightness; coming and going are mutually dependent, forming the meaning of the Middle Way. All remaining questions are all like this. You who are to transmit the Dharma hereafter should teach by turning this over and over, and not lose the essential purport!”

blocks.text: 4. Desiring to Leave the World

inline.s: In the first year of the Taiji era (renzi), in the seventh month of the Yanhe period, the Master commanded his disciples to go to the Guoen Monastery in Xinzhou to build a stupa, and urged that the work be hastened. In the following year, at the end of summer, it was completed. On the first day of the seventh month he gathered the assembly and said: “In the eighth month I wish to leave the world. If you have doubts, ask me early, and I will resolve them for you and let your confusion be entirely ended. After I am gone, no one will teach you!” Hearing this, Fahai and the others all wept; only Shenhui was unmoved in his spirit, and did not weep.

The Master said: “The young master Shenhui alone has attained the equality of good and evil, is unmoved by slander and praise, and gives rise to neither grief nor joy. The rest of you have not attained this. After years in the mountains, what Way have you cultivated? Why do you grieve and weep now — for whom is the anxiety? If you grieve that I do not know where I am going, I know where I am going; if I did not know where I am going, I would not have told you in advance. Your weeping is because you do not know where I go; if you knew where I go, you would not weep. For the Dharma-nature is originally without arising or ceasing, without coming or going.”

blocks.text: 5. The Verse on True and False, Motion and Stillness

inline.s: Sit down, all of you, and I will speak to you a verse called the ‘Verse on True and False, Motion and Stillness.’ When you have learned and recited this verse, you will be of one mind with me; practicing in accord with it, you will not lose the essential purport!”
The assembled monks paid their respects and asked the Master to compose the verse. The verse says:
In all things there is nothing true; do not take it for the seeing of the true;
If one sees it as the true, what he sees is altogether not true.
If one can possess the true of himself, apart from the false the mind is true;
If the self-mind does not leave the false, where is the true to be found in what has no truth?
Sentient beings are those who comprehend motion; the insentient are those without motion;
If one practices the practice of immobility, he is the same as the insentient, without motion.
If you seek the true immobility, in motion there is immobility;
If immobility is just immobility, then the insentient have no seed of Buddhahood.
Able to distinguish the marks well, in the truth of the First Meaning there is no motion;
But if you have such a view, that is the function of Suchness.
I tell all who study the Way: make effort and be attentive;
Do not, at the gate of the Mahayana, cling to the wisdom of birth and death.
If at the words there is correspondence, then together discuss the meaning of the Buddha;
If in truth there is no correspondence, put palms together and let the other be glad.
This school is originally without contention; contention is to lose the meaning of the Way;
To cling to the perverse Dharma-door of contention, one’s self-nature enters birth and death.”

At that time, having heard the verse, the assembly of followers all paid their respects and, comprehending the Master’s meaning, each gathered his mind and practiced in accord with the Dharma, daring no longer to contend.

blocks.text: 6. The Platform Sutra of the Dharma Treasure

inline.s: Then they knew the Master would not long remain in the world. The Elder Fahai bowed again and asked: “After the Master’s nirvana, to whom shall the robe and the Dharma be entrusted?” The Master said: “When I spoke the Dharma at the Dafan Monastery up to the present, the record has been copied and circulated, and is called the Platform Sutra of the Dharma Treasure. You should guard it and transmit it to one another, delivering all beings; as long as you expound in accord with this, it is called the true Dharma. Now I speak the Dharma for you, but I no longer bequeath the robe, because the root of your faith is pure and ripe, your determination beyond doubt, worthy to shoulder the great matter. Yet according to the verse of entrustment of the ancestor Bodhidharma, the robe should not be transmitted. The verse says:”
I originally came to this land, transmitting the Dharma to save the deluded;
One flower opens into five leaves; the fruit is naturally accomplished.”

blocks.text: 7. The Single Mark and the Single Practice

inline.s: The Master further said: “Good friends! Each of you should purify your mind and listen to my speaking the Dharma. If you wish to accomplish the wisdom of all species, you must reach the samadhi of the single mark and the samadhi of the single practice. If in all places you do not dwell in marks, and in those marks give rise to neither hatred nor love, have neither grasping nor rejection, and do not think of benefit, success, or failure and the like, being at ease, tranquil, void, calm, and indifferent — this is called the samadhi of the single mark. If in all places, whether walking, standing, sitting, or lying, you maintain a single straightforward mind, with an unmoved place of the Way and truly accomplish the Pure Land — this is called the samadhi of the single practice. If a person is endowed with these two samadhis, it is like the earth having the seed, which conceals, nourishes, and matures its fruit. The single mark and the single practice are likewise.”

The Dharma I now speak is like the timely rain that universally moistens the great earth; and your Buddha-nature is likened to the seeds, which, meeting this saturation, all sprout. One who receives my purport will certainly attain bodhi; one who practices according to my words will surely realize the wonderful fruit. Listen to my verse:”
The mind-ground contains all the seeds; by the universal rain all sprout;
When the flower of sudden awakening has already so come, the fruit of bodhi is naturally accomplished.”

Having spoken the verse, the Master said: “The Dharma is non-dual, and the mind is likewise so. The Way is pure and also without all marks. Take care not to contemplate stillness, nor to empty the mind; this mind is originally pure, and there is nothing to grasp or reject. Each of you make effort on your own, and, according to conditions, fare well!” At that time the assembled followers paid their respects and withdrew.

blocks.text: 8. The Falling Leaf Returns to the Root

inline.s: On the eighth day of the seventh month, the Master suddenly said to his disciples: “I wish to return to Xinzhou; you should quickly prepare the boat.” The assembly entreated him to remain with great earnestness. The Master said: “Even the Buddhas, appearing in the world, still show nirvana; where there is coming there must be going, and this is the constant principle. This body of mine must have a place to return.” The assembly said: “Master, going from here, will you return soon?” The Master said: “The falling leaf returns to the root; and when I come again, I have no words.” They asked again: “To whom is the true eye-treasury of the Dharma entrusted?” The Master said: “The one who has the Way obtains it; the one who is without mind is versed in it.”

They asked again: “In the future, will there be any peril?” The Master said: “Five or six years after my nirvana, a person will come to take my head. Hear my prophecy: On the head one nurses the parents; in the mouth one needs food. The peril of ‘Man’; the officials of ‘Poplar and Willow.’” Again he said: “Seventy years after I am gone, two bodhisattvas will come from the East, one a renunciant and one a householder; at the same time they will spread the teaching, establish my school, build monasteries, and make the Dharma-succession flourish.”

blocks.text: 9. The Lineage of the Chan School

inline.s: They asked: “We do not know how many generations have been transmitted, from the historically manifested Buddhas and patriarchs down to the present. We beg the Master to disclose it.” The Master said: “The ancient Buddhas who appeared in the world were already without number and cannot be counted. Now we take the seven Buddhas as the beginning. In the past kalpa of Splendor: Vipashyin Buddha, Shikhin Buddha, and Vishvabhu Buddha; in the present kalpa of the Wise: Krakucchanda Buddha, Kanakamuni Buddha, Kashyapa Buddha, and Shakyamuni Buddha — these are the seven Buddhas.”

Shakyamuni Buddha first transmitted to the Venerable Mahakashyapa; second, the Venerable Ananda; third, the Venerable Shanavasa; fourth, the Venerable Upagupta; fifth, the Venerable Dhritaka; sixth, the Venerable Micchaka; seventh, the Venerable Vasumitra; eighth, the Venerable Buddhanandi; ninth, the Venerable Buddhamitra; tenth, the Venerable Parsva; eleventh, the Venerable Punyayashas; twelfth, the Great Being Ashvaghosha; thirteenth, the Venerable Kapimala; fourteenth, the Great Being Nagarjuna; fifteenth, the Venerable Kanadeva; sixteenth, the Venerable Rahulata; seventeenth, the Venerable Sanghanandi; eighteenth, the Venerable Gayashata; nineteenth, the Venerable Kumarata; twentieth, the Venerable Jayata; twenty-first, the Venerable Vasubandhu; twenty-second, the Venerable Manorhita; twenty-third, the Venerable Haklenayashas; twenty-fourth, the Venerable Simha; twenty-fifth, the Venerable Basiasita; twenty-sixth, the Venerable Punyamitra; twenty-seventh, the Venerable Prajnatara; twenty-eighth, the Venerable Bodhidharma; twenty-ninth, the great master Huike; thirtieth, the great master Sengcan; thirty-first, the great master Daoxin; thirty-second, the great master Hongren; and Huineng is the thirty-third patriarch. The patriarchs of old each had their transmission. You, in the generations to come, should pass it down from teacher to teacher and not err!”

blocks.text: 10. I Take Leave of You

inline.s: In the Xiantian era, second year (guichou), on the third day of the eighth month, after the meal at the Guoen Monastery, the Master said to his disciples: “Take your places in order, and I will take leave of you.”
Fahai said: “Master, what teaching will you leave, so that the deluded people of later generations may see their Buddha-nature?”

The Master said: “Listen carefully! If the deluded people of later ages recognize sentient beings, that is their Buddha-nature; if they do not recognize sentient beings, then in ten thousand kalpas seeking the Buddha they will hardly encounter him. I now teach you: recognize the sentient beings of your own mind and see the Buddha-nature of your own mind. If you seek to see the Buddha, just recognize sentient beings; for it is only that sentient beings are deluded about the Buddha, not that the Buddha is deluded about sentient beings. If the self-nature awakens, sentient beings are the Buddha; if the self-nature is deluded, the Buddha is sentient beings. If the self-nature is equal, sentient beings are the Buddha; if the self-nature is evil and dangerous, the Buddha is sentient beings. If your mind is dangerous and crooked, then the Buddha is amid sentient beings; with a single thought of straight and even, sentient beings are the Buddha. My own mind has the Buddha in itself; this self-Buddha is the true Buddha. If the self lacks the Buddha-mind, where will you seek a real Buddha? Your self-mind is the Buddha; do not doubt it further. Outside there is no single thing that can be established; all the ten thousand dharmas are born from the original mind. Therefore the Sutra says: When the mind arises, all manner of dharmas arise; when the mind ceases, all manner of dharmas cease.”

blocks.text: 11. The Verse on the True Buddha of Self-Nature

inline.s: I now leave a verse to take leave of you, called the ‘Verse on the True Buddha of Self-Nature.’ People of later generations, knowing the meaning of this verse, will see their own original mind and accomplish their own path of Buddhahood. The verse says:
Suchness, the self-nature, is the true Buddha; erroneous views and the three poisons are the devil king;
When deluded by error, the devil is in the house; when right views are present, the Buddha is in the hall.
When erroneous views and the three poisons arise in the nature, that is the devil king coming to dwell in the house;
With right views the mind of the three poisons is naturally removed; the devil becomes the Buddha, truly without falsehood.
The Dharma-body, the reward-body, and the transformation-body — these three bodies are originally one body;
If you can see it for yourself within the nature, that is the cause of becoming a Buddha, of bodhi.
Originally from the transformation-body the pure nature is born; the pure nature is always within the transformation-body;
If the nature makes the transformation-body walk the right path, in the future it will be perfected and truly endless.
The nature of lust is originally the cause of the pure nature; apart from lust is the body of the pure nature;
In the nature, when one is freed from the five desires, to see the nature in an instant is to be the true.
In this life, if one meets the gate of the sudden teaching and suddenly awakens to the self-nature, he sees the World-Honored One;
If you seek to practice and find how to become a Buddha, do you know where to seek the true?
If you can see the true within the mind, having the true is the cause of becoming a Buddha;
If you do not see the self-nature and seek the Buddha outside, then whoever raises the mind is always the great fool.
The gate of the sudden teaching is now left behind; to save and deliver the world’s people one must cultivate oneself;
I tell you who are to study the Way in the future: not to have this view is a great remissness.”

blocks.text: 12. Causing You to See Your Nature

inline.s: Having spoken the verse, the Master announced: “Dwell well, all of you! After my nirvana, do not indulge in the world’s grief and shed streaming tears. To receive condolement and put on mourning clothes — such a one is not my disciple, nor is it the true Dharma. Just know your original mind and see your original nature, which is without motion or stillness, without arising or ceasing, without coming or going, without right or wrong, without abiding or departing. I fear that your minds are deluded and will not comprehend my meaning, so I instruct you again, to cause you to see your nature. After my nirvana, practice according to this, exactly as when I was in the world; if you go against my teaching, then even if I were in the world, there would be no benefit.”
Again he spoke a verse, saying:
Unmoved, one does not cultivate good; unrestrained, one does not commit evil;
Still and silent, cutting off seeing and hearing; vast and free, the mind has no attachment.

blocks.text: 13. The White Rainbow Reaching the Ground

inline.s: Having spoken the verse, the Master sat upright until the third watch of the night. Suddenly he said to his disciples: “I go now!” and, calmly, he passed away. At that time rare incense filled the chamber, a white rainbow reached the ground, the trees and woods turned white, and the birds and beasts cried out in grief.

In the eleventh month, the officials of the three prefectures — Guangzhou, Shaozhou, and Xinzhou — together with the disciples, monks, and laypeople, contended to receive the true body, unable to decide where it should go; so they burned incense and prayed: “Wherever the incense-smoke points, there shall the Master abide.” At that time the smoke of the incense went straight through toward Caoxi. On the thirteenth day of the eleventh month, they moved the spirit-shrine together with the transmitted robe and bowl and returned.

In the following year, on the twenty-fifth day of the seventh month, they opened the shrine, and the disciple Fangbian applied fragrant clay to the body. The disciples, recalling the prophecy about the taking of the head, first protected the Master’s neck with iron leaves and lacquered cloth, and entered it into the stupa. Suddenly within the stupa a white light appeared, rising straight up into the sky, and only dispersed after three days. The prefecture of Shaozhou reported it to the throne, and an imperial edict was issued to erect a stele recording the Master’s virtuous conduct.

The Master lived to seventy-six. At twenty-four he received the robe; at thirty-nine he shaved his head; and he spoke the Dharma to benefit beings for thirty-seven years. Those who obtained his purport and succeeded to the Dharma numbered forty-three; those who awakened to the Way and transcended the ordinary were beyond counting. The faithful robe transmitted by Bodhidharma, the woolen and jeweled bowl bestowed by Emperor Zhongzong, the true portrait sculpted by Fangbian, and the implements — these the keeper of the stupa preserved, to be forever safeguarded at the Baolin way-place. The Platform Sutra was circulated in order to reveal the essential purport. All these are matters that caused the Triple Gem to flourish and universally benefited all beings.
